properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-20 in the SHIPPED v0.65.0 binary: the only worked example for add_contributor's `id` is `who:ajs`, a real private individual and a real row in this project's own contributor table — served verbatim into every project reflow2 is installed in
properties.statement: SYMPTOM AS REPORTED, second-hand and not yet measured at the source: on a separate reflow2 design at Anthony's brother's workplace, the contributor "ajs" appears on many nodes. Anthony has never worked on that project. WHAT WAS MEASURED HERE, 2026-09-20, against the SHIPPED artifacts rather than the working tree. The published kit tarball contains no occurrence of the string "ajs" anywhere. The published linux binary contains five, all of them in text the server SERVES to every client: add_contributor's `id` parameter reads "Stable id (e.g. `who:ajs`, `who:claude-code`)"; its `handle` parameter offers "(`@ajs`)"; Constraint.limit_source, served by describe_schema, offers "the Contributor who asserted it (`who:ajs`, `who:claude-code`)"; and Snapshot.target_id recounts "ctr:anthony merged into who:ajs". All four are real rows in THIS project's own contributor table: who:ajs is Anthony Sligar with handle @ajs, and who:claude-code is a real Contributor too. So the single worked example an agent reads at the exact moment it invents a contributor id is a named private individual's real id. TWO CANDIDATES REMAIN AND THEY ARE DISTINGUISHABLE. (C) An agent on that machine followed the served example and wrote who:ajs for somebody else, in which case the id now denotes two different people in two graphs. (D) That graph absorbed Anthony's nodes wholesale, through import_graph, merge_designs, a copied .reflow2/graph, or the git-pull-the-design-rules workflow Anthony has described wanting, in which case who:ajs correctly denotes him and simply should not be there. THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, two calls on the brother's graph, which nobody here can take: read who:ajs and look at its name and description. "Anthony Sligar" with the long systems-engineer persona means D. The brother's own name, a colleague's, or a blank one means C, which is the worse reading because the identity has forked. Then scan for Project nodes: if reflow2's own project or requirements are present, D is settled regardless. REFUTED IN SOURCE, so it is not a third candidate: the server never creates a Contributor by itself and never derives an identity from the environment, the git config or the OS user. claim_region explicitly REFUSES an unknown contributor id rather than minting one, and no env::var on USER or LOGNAME exists in either crate. Nothing can put a name in a graph that an agent or an import did not put there. THE CLASS IS LARGER THAN ONE NAME. The served surface draws its worked examples from real projects, and who:ajs is only the instance that was noticed. @ajs is a second. Constraint.limit_source also offers `art:ifc-shell-model` and `ifc_quantify`, which are bhome's artifact and an IfcMCP tool — a different customer's identifiers, shipped to everybody. A fix that changes who:ajs alone leaves the class open, and the class is what makes this a privacy question rather than a typo: reflow2 is a wrench for other people's projects, and its examples are currently drawn from the hands that made it. WHAT WOULD PIN IT: a gate asserting that no served tool or schema description contains a Contributor id, handle or display name that this project's own graph holds. That is checkable from the export plus the served surface, it would have failed on the day the example was written, and it is the same shape as the surface-enumerating gates the crate already carries. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether C or D is actually the case at the brother's site; the exact wording of the report, which reached here paraphrased; whether any OTHER project has the same contributor; and whether an agent demonstrably copies this example, which is a behavioural claim no static reading can settle.
